# 1 Kings Chapter 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Just then, a man of God arrived from Judah at Bethel, sent by the word of the LORD. Jeroboam was standing at the altar, about to make an offering.

**2** The man cried out against the altar by the LORD's command: "Altar! Altar! This is what the LORD says: 'A son will be born to David's dynasty — his name will be Josiah — and on you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn offerings on you. Human bones will be burned on you.'"

**3** That same day the man gave a confirming sign: "This is the proof that the LORD has spoken: this altar will split apart, and the ashes on it will spill out."

**4** When King Jeroboam heard the man of God's words against the altar at Bethel, he pointed at him from the altar and ordered, "Arrest him!" But the hand he stretched out shriveled up, and he couldn't pull it back.

**5** The altar split apart and the ashes spilled out, exactly as the sign the man of God had announced by the LORD's word.

**6** The king pleaded with the man of God, "Please pray to the LORD your God for me — ask him to restore my hand." The man of God prayed, and the king's hand was restored to normal.

**7** The king said to the man of God, "Come home with me for a meal. I'll give you a gift."

**8** But the man of God told the king, "Even if you gave me half of everything you own, I would not go with you, and I would not eat or drink anything here.

**9** The LORD gave me strict orders: 'Do not eat bread, do not drink water, and do not return by the same route you came.'"

**10** So he took a different road and did not go back the way he had come to Bethel.

**11** Now an old prophet was living in Bethel. His sons came and told him everything the man of God had done in Bethel that day and what he had said to the king.

**12** Their father asked, "Which road did he take?" His sons had watched which direction the man of God from Judah had gone.

**13** He told his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." They did, and he mounted it.

**14** He caught up with the man of God, who was sitting under an oak tree. "Are you the man of God from Judah?" he asked. "I am," the man replied.

**15** "Come home with me and have a meal," the prophet said.

**16** "I can't go back with you or join you," the man replied. "I can't eat or drink anything with you here,

**17** because the LORD told me, 'Do not eat bread or drink water there. Do not go back the way you came.'"

**18** The old prophet said, "I'm a prophet too, just like you. And an angel told me by the LORD's word, 'Bring him home with you and give him food and water.'" He was lying.

**19** So the man of God went back with him, and ate and drank at his house.

**20** While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back.

**21** He announced to the man of God from Judah, "This is what the LORD says: 'You have defied the word of the LORD and disobeyed the command the LORD your God gave you.

**22** You came back and ate and drank in the place he told you not to. Therefore your body will not be buried in your family tomb.'"

**23** After the man of God had eaten and drunk, the old prophet saddled the donkey for him.

**24** As he traveled, a lion met him on the road and killed him. His body lay on the road, with both the donkey and the lion standing beside it.

**25** Some passersby saw the body lying on the road with the lion standing next to it. They went and reported it in the town where the old prophet lived.

**26** When the prophet who had brought him back heard about it, he said, "It is the man of God who defied the LORD's command. The LORD gave him over to the lion, which mauled and killed him, just as the LORD had warned him."

**27** He told his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me," and they did.

**28** He went out and found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and the lion still standing beside it. The lion had neither eaten the body nor attacked the donkey.

**29** The prophet picked up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to the town to mourn for him and bury him.

**30** He placed the body in his own tomb, and they mourned over him, crying, "Oh, my brother!"

**31** After the burial, he told his sons, "When I die, bury me in the same tomb as the man of God. Lay my bones right next to his.

**32** Because the message he proclaimed by the LORD's authority against the altar in Bethel and against all the hilltop shrines in the towns of Samaria will certainly come true."

**33** Even after all this, Jeroboam did not change his ways. He continued appointing anyone who wanted the job as priests for the high places.

**34** This became the sin that led to the downfall and total destruction of Jeroboam's dynasty.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **13:2 — Josiah named**: The prophet names a king who won't be born for three hundred years. This is the most specific predictive prophecy in the Hebrew Bible, and its fulfillment in 2 Kings 23:15-16 is presented as exact. The narrative stakes its credibility on this kind of claim.

2. **13:18 — "He was lying"**: Three words that make this one of the most disturbing stories in the Bible. A genuine prophet deliberately deceives another prophet. The man of God believes the lie because it comes from a fellow prophet — and pays with his life for believing it. The story asks: how do you know when a religious authority is lying to you?

3. **13:24-28 — the impossible scene**: A lion stands next to a donkey and a corpse without eating either. This is not nature; this is theater. God has staged a tableau that can only be read as supernatural judgment. The lion is not hunting — it is making a point.

4. **13:33 — "did not change his ways"**: The chapter's bitter conclusion. A miraculous sign, a withered hand restored, an altar destroyed, a prophet killed by a lion — and Jeroboam continues exactly as before. The hardened heart is the real subject of this chapter.

— PNEUMA
